title: cuda-symbol-version-mismatch-notes
content:
Context:
Personal debugging scratchpad — intermittent failures when launching containers that use torch/transformers. Symptoms vary: sometimes OOM at token-generation time, sometimes immediate failure on import with an undefined-symbol / version not found error (seen when loading libtorch/libcudart). Suspect driver vs runtime mismatches, or mixed libcuda on host vs container.

System snapshot (host):
- Host: ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15.0-76-generic
- GPUs: 1x A100-SXM4-80GB (driver visible as NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.13)
- nvidia-smi (host):
  Wed Feb 17 14:02:58 2026
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.13 Driver Version: 525.60.13 CUDA Version: 12.1 |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Container images tried:
- nvidia/cuda:11.8-base (baseline)
- pytorch/pytorch:1.13-cuda11.7-cudnn8-runtime
- custom runtime image built from base with conda env (cudatoolkit=11.7)

Common commands run and outputs (trimmed):
1) docker run check libcuda visibility
$ docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi\N+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.13 Driver Version: 525.60.13 CUDA Version: 12.1 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
=> Host driver visible in container (good)

2) quick python import check inside container (pytorch image)
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
Expected: 11.7 / True
Actual (failing run):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/__init__.py", line 83, in <module>
    from .lib import *
  File "/opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/lib/__init__.py", line 144, in <module>
    torch._C = _load_lib('_C', 'torch._C')
  File "/opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/lib/__init__.py", line 129, in _load_lib
    lib = ctypes.CDLL(os.path.join(lib_dir, filename), RTLD_GLOBAL | RTLD_NOW)
  FileNotFoundError: /opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/lib/libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file: version `CUDA_11.0' not found

Notes: error mentions version `CUDA_11.0' not found which is odd given the image uses 11.7 packages. Suggests symbol/version versioned SONAME mismatch inside baked wheel or conda package.

3) ldd /path/to/libtorch.so (inside container)\$ ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so\  ...
  libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f4caa2c3000)
  libcudart.so.11.0 => not found

Host ldconfig shows libcuda points to host driver version, but libcudart missing inside container unless provided by cudatoolkit package.

4) strace on python import (short run):
- shows attempts to open /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 -> ENOENT
- falls back to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.11 but versioned symbol mismatch later

Observed kernel/dmesg OOM traces (when OOM occurs):
- [  214.104676] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:3A:00.0 has fallen off the bus.
- [  214.104679] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3a:00): 13, pid=4222, tid=4222, 0xffffffffc0000008
- Segfaults and kernel logs imply possible driver panics when library mismatches cause invalid ioctl sequences.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Mixed CUDA runtime symbols: wheel/conda package built against CUDA 11.0/11.1 but running against host driver providing newer/older ABI -> undefined symbol/version errors.
2) Container image missing matched libcudart (conda cudatoolkit not present, or mismatched minor), causing torch to attempt linking to unavailable SONAME -> import failure.
3) Driver bug triggered on A100 with mismatched user-space libs -> GPU falls off bus and kernel reports Xid 13. This matches past incidents where user libs attempted unsupported ioctls.
4) OOM cases separate: real memory pressure during generation, exacerbated by incorrect environment (e.g., DEBUG builds, nonvlink->large JITs).

Commands tried to remediate (and notes):
- Ensured docker run maps host driver libs: tested with --volume /usr/local/nvidia:/usr/local/nvidia:ro -> made libcuda visible but did not provide libcudart inside container (still missing).
- Installed conda cudatoolkit=11.7 inside container -> fixed libcudart presence, import succeeds in many cases, but intermittent Xid 31 still occurs under load.
- Switched to pytorch wheel built for CUDA 11.8; still had version tags complaining about CUDA_11.0 when using older torch wheel. Conclusion: must match wheel to installed cudatoolkit.
- Rebooted host, updated driver to 525.73.01 (later run) -> reduced "fall off the bus" events but not eliminated.
- Tried setting LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1: no effect for import errors; that only helped NVML visibility in some stacks.
- ldd shows several libs pointing at /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 (libcuda) while libcudart is resolved from conda env; mixing host and env runtimes seems fragile.

Repro script notes (to reproduce locally):
- Build container: FROM nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime-ubuntu22.04
- conda install -c pytorch pytorch=1.13 cudatoolkit=11.7 -y
- python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); import transformers; ...'
- Sometimes import fails with FileNotFoundError for libcudart.so.11.0; sometimes succeeds but later OOMs on small batches (~B=1, seq_len=1024) when model is a 7B fp16.

Next investigation steps (todo):
- Rebuild minimal repro image pinned to exact cudatoolkit and pytorch wheel versions (avoid conda meta mismatch). Document exact versions that work.
- Capture full dmesg and journalctl -k when Xid and fall-off-bus occur; escalate to infra if kernel driver logs show consistent panic.
- Try mounting host /usr/local/cuda into container to provide unified user-space CUDA libs (but be careful; can introduce incompatibility with driver).
- Run same workload on a smaller GPU (RTX A6000) to see if issue is specific to A100 drivers.
- Try nvidia-container-runtime v3 vs v2; sometimes runtime changes how libcuda is exposed.
- For OOM: instrument memory with torch.cuda.memory_stats() and limit batch sizes and token chunking; add prefix-caching to reduce peak allocation.

Notes to self (less formal):
- Remember: libcuda from host driver is *not* the same as libcudart from cudatoolkit inside container; both must be ABI compatible. The versioned symbol errors (CUDA_11.0 not found) usually mean the wheel expects an older libcudart symbol table.
- In the past we pinned working combo: driver 525.x + cudatoolkit 11.7 + pytorch 1.13 built for 11.7. Keep that matrix in runtime docs.
- If we can't get stable behavior, consider moving heavy inference to dedicated nodes with matched validated images and stricter image policy (no mixing conda wheel + host libcuda mismatch).

Bookmarks / useful references:
- https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/cuda-compatibility/
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker/issues/1326 (notes on libcuda in container)
- Internal PR: runtime/pull/314 — changes to container entrypoint to assert cuda libs present

End of scratchpad.
